subject: Request: proportionate overrun allocation & temporary rate hold
messages:
From: Marta Gomez <finance@brightsource.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected overrun from June 9-11 — invoice query

Hi Olga,

We received the June invoice this morning and theres a ~42% overrun compared to our forecast for the June 9-11 launch window. Our engineering team confirms the spike was caused by temporary A/B testing that drove very short, high-frequency bursts. We understand surge protections exist, but the size of this charge will materially impact our Q2 cash planning.

Can Redwood provide an allocation path or a mitigation offer? Specifically: 1) can you split the overrun costs with us given this was a short experimental window, and 2) is there a short-term rate hold available while we finalize a PO to increase committed capacity?

Ive attached a quick export of our usage for the period. Happy to jump on a call today if that helps.

Thanks,
Marta Gomez
VP, Finance — BrightSource
attachments: usage_report_q2.csv (csv)
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example>
To: Marta Gomez <finance@brightsource.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected overrun from June 9-11 — invoice query

Hi Marta,

Thanks for flagging this and for the usage exportthat was helpful. Sorry for the surprise on your end. Weve reviewed the logs and confirm the pattern was short-duration, high-frequency calls consistent with A/B traffic. Given the one-off nature, Id like to propose a compromise to avoid blowing up your quarter:

- Proportional overrun allocation: Redwood would absorb 60% of the overrun amount attributable to June 9-11, BrightSource would be billed 40%. (Were willing to make this exception for this single launch window.)
- Amortization: any remaining billed overrun can be amortized over the next 3 monthly invoices to reduce immediate cash impact.
- Temporary rate hold: we can hold BrightSource at your current committed per-token rate for 30 days while you finalize the PO for increased committed capacity. After 30 days, the rate would revert unless a PO is in place.

Im looping in Ben (Account) and Laura (CS) to confirm feasibility from pricing and implementation. Ive attached a short draft that shows the amortization math and proposed amendment language. If this looks OK, we can route for a quick legal tweak and DocuSign.

Next steps I propose: Ben to sign off on the concession; Laura to confirm how we reflect amortization on invoices; then legal to issue a 1-paragraph amendment for signatures.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Sr. Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed_amortization_term.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example>, Marta Gomez <finance@brightsource.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected overrun from June 9-11 — invoice query

Thanks Olgaand Marta. I support Olgas proposal with a small clarification on the economics: Redwood absorbs 60% of the direct overrun token charges for the 9-11 window (we will not apply any surcharge on top of that share), and BrightSource is billed 40% but that 40% is amortized over 3 months (equal installments on next 3 invoices).

Operational notes: Laura, can your team emit an invoice line item labeled June launch amortized overrun (3mo) so BrightSources finance team can easily match? Jonas, can Legal review the suggested 1-paragraph amendment to confirm were not creating precedent beyond this single waived/absorbed instance?

If legal is comfortable, Im OK to approve the temporary rate hold for 30 days provided we get a PO in that window and a signature on the amendment. Marta—if you can confirm PO timing, well lock the current rate immediately.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example>, Marta Gomez <finance@brightsource.com>

Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 14:03:00 -0700

Ben/Olga/Marta,

Otherwise the terms are standard.

Ive drafted the one-paragraph amendment in Word and attached it as redwood_amendment_draft.docx. If Marta and BrightSource procurement agree, I can push this through DocuSign and include a checkbox for the 3-month amortization schedule and PO reference number. Link below (temporary envelope).
